perspective:
Harold Padilla’s available information:

- He is a project manager. He has a friendly/professional relationship with Arthur Begum and often seeks Arthur’s advice.
- In the coffee-shop meeting, Harold feels frustrated and anxious because he believes his project team is unmotivated and this is hurting progress. He tells Arthur this. He hears Arthur advise him to understand each team member’s individual motivation, have one-on-one conversations, and make people feel valued and understood. Harold decides to try this and feels hopeful.
- He tells his team he wants one-on-one chats to learn what motivates them. He hears Team Member 1 say this could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. He says he will schedule time with each person and wants the project to succeed together.
- After implementing the advice, Harold observes that the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried about the project’s future. He tells Arthur this. He hears Arthur suggest there may be deeper issues such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold decides to set up another round of meetings.
- In deeper one-on-one meetings, Harold asks team members to share concerns or problems. He hears Team Member 1 say there is tension among a few people affecting work. He hears Team Member 2 say they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts, redistribute tasks, and that their well-being matters.
- Harold feels optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns will improve performance. He tells the team he will create a more supportive, open environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He hears Team Member 1 say that sounds great/helpful and Team Member 2 agree that their concerns are being addressed. Harold says he is glad and emphasizes that their input and well-being are crucial to success.

He does not have access to other characters’ private thoughts, hidden motives, narrator-only details, or events he did not observe.
